I am 71 years old and this small plot of 0.09 hectares is all I have in Dodoma, where the rains are short and unreliable. I intercrop sorghum and groundnuts here using seeds I saved from last season, because I cannot afford to buy new seeds or chemical fertilizer from town. I spread cow dung on the plot when my neighbor's livestock pass by, but I do not spray any chemicals and I have no way to irrigate— we simply wait for the rains. The plot is small enough that my grandchildren and I can manage the planting, weeding, and harvesting ourselves without hiring anyone.
